cc_wm15_annoying.title: File:Wikimania 2015 - Luis Von Ahn - Bringing Free Education to the World.webm
cc_wm15_annoying.author: Wikimedia México
cc_wm15_annoying.words: How many of you found it really annoying? Excellent. Okay. Well, I invented that. Sorry.

cc_wm15_feelbad.title: File:Wikimania 2015 - Luis Von Ahn - Bringing Free Education to the World.webm
cc_wm15_feelbad.author: Wikimedia México
cc_wm15_feelbad.words: And if you multiply 10 seconds by 200 million, you get that humanity as a whole is wasting about 500,000 hours every day typing these annoying CAPTCHAs because of me. So, I started feeling bad.

cc_wm15_free.title: File:Wikimania 2015 - Luis Von Ahn - Bringing Free Education to the World.webm
cc_wm15_free.author: Wikimedia México
cc_wm15_free.words: So, what I wanted to do is I wanted to make something that would teach people languages, but it was entirely free. And this is what we did with Duolingo.

cc_v3_bots.title: File:Introducing reCAPTCHA v3.webm
cc_v3_bots.author: Google Search Central
cc_v3_bots.words: If you have a website, you need to protect your users from bots. Bots are trying leaked passwords, hosting spam, and scraping your content.

cc_v3_score.title: File:Introducing reCAPTCHA v3.webm
cc_v3_score.author: Google Search Central
cc_v3_score.words: reCAPTCHA v3 does away with the need for interactive tests and gives you a score to let you know when you have risky traffic.

cc_v3_signals.title: File:Introducing reCAPTCHA v3.webm
cc_v3_signals.author: Google Search Central
cc_v3_signals.words: reCAPTCHA's adaptive risk analysis engine takes in various signals about the interaction and predicts the likelihood that the request was generated by a bot.

cc_v3_places.title: File:Introducing reCAPTCHA v3.webm
cc_v3_places.author: Google Search Central
cc_v3_places.words: It works best with context about how both humans and bots interact with your website, so for best performance, include reCAPTCHA in many places.

cc_v3_catfood.title: File:Introducing reCAPTCHA v3.webm
cc_v3_catfood.author: Google Search Central
cc_v3_catfood.words: Here was a bot posting a review for a competitor's cat food.

cc_wm15_scalpers.title: File:Wikimania 2015 - Luis Von Ahn - Bringing Free Education to the World.webm
cc_wm15_scalpers.author: Wikimedia México
cc_wm15_scalpers.words: So, for example, in the case of Ticketmaster, the reason you have to type these characters is to prevent scalpers from writing a program that can buy millions of tickets two at a time.

cc_wm15_brain.title: File:Wikimania 2015 - Luis Von Ahn - Bringing Free Education to the World.webm
cc_wm15_brain.author: Wikimedia México
cc_wm15_brain.words: See, during those 10 seconds, while you're typing a CAPTCHA, your brain is doing something amazing. Your brain is doing something that computers cannot yet do.

cc_wm15_agree.title: File:Wikimania 2015 - Luis Von Ahn - Bringing Free Education to the World.webm
cc_wm15_agree.author: Wikimedia México
cc_wm15_agree.words: And if we repeat this process to like 10 different people, and they all agree on what the new word is, then we get one more word digitized with very high accuracy.

cc_wm15_books.title: File:Wikimania 2015 - Luis Von Ahn - Bringing Free Education to the World.webm
cc_wm15_books.author: Wikimedia México
cc_wm15_books.words: It has been very successful. Today, this is digitizing approximately 100 million words a day, which is the equivalent of about 2 million books a year.

cc_wm15_billion.title: File:Wikimania 2015 - Luis Von Ahn - Bringing Free Education to the World.webm
cc_wm15_billion.author: Wikimedia México
cc_wm15_billion.words: This is 1.1 billion. This is the total number of distinct people that have ever helped us digitize at least one word out of a book through the system. It's about 15% of the world's population.

cc_v3_checkbox.title: File:Introducing reCAPTCHA v3.webm
cc_v3_checkbox.author: Google Search Central
cc_v3_checkbox.words: The reCAPTCHA I'm not a robot checkbox changed the way to protect your websites, but its one-time verification doesn't fit every use case. reCAPTCHA v3 does away with the need for interactive tests and gives you a score to let you know when you have risky traffic.

cc_s34_history.title: Humans as Software Extensions (34C3, talk 9077)
cc_s34_history.author: Sebastian Schmieg · Chaos Computer Club (media.ccc.de)
cc_s34_history.words: So, if you look at it, captchas started as a technique to merely prevent spam. And then, they kind of morphed into a method for deciphering house numbers and transcribing books. And then, lately, it's become a means of teaching image recognition to AI software.

cc_s34_lawsuit.title: Humans as Software Extensions (34C3, talk 9077)
cc_s34_lawsuit.author: Sebastian Schmieg · Chaos Computer Club (media.ccc.de)
cc_s34_lawsuit.words: And she claimed that Google operates a highly profitable transcription business built upon free labor, which it deceptively and unfairly obtains from unwitting website users.

cc_s34_unpaid.title: Humans as Software Extensions (34C3, talk 9077)
cc_s34_unpaid.author: Sebastian Schmieg · Chaos Computer Club (media.ccc.de)
cc_s34_unpaid.words: So, you can automate as much as you want, but at some point you will have to train and especially maintain the machines and the software. So, I would say AI creates yet another layer of badly or unpaid care and maintenance work, which is often invisible on purpose.

cc_f36_maria.title: Inside the Fake Like Factories (36C3, talk 10936)
cc_f36_maria.author: Svea Eckert, Philip Kreissel, Dennis Tatang · Chaos Computer Club (media.ccc.de)
cc_f36_maria.words: So Maria is a former police officer. And as money is always short, she is clicking Facebook likes for money. So she earns between two cents and six cents per like.

cc_k35_bot.title: Toll of personal privacy in 2018 (35C3 Chaos West, talk 32)
cc_k35_bot.author: Kirils Solovjovs · Chaos Computer Club (media.ccc.de)
cc_k35_bot.words: So I was accepting and honoring all cookies before, and now I only accept temporarily first-party cookies. And big tracking giants do not like that. So they make my life difficult. They think I'm a bot. I don't have any internet history associated with me.
